cases.reason: The value rule is word-identical, but in 2002 the returned value of this integer function is governed by 15.3.1 (an uncatalogued 2002 clause) in two modes: native, and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, where the value is held in a 32-digit standard intermediate data item. A boolean argument can exceed 32 digits (PIC 1(110) USAGE BIT = 2**110-1, 34 digits). The 2023 row's evidence covers native/standard-decimal only; the twin's witness does not run at 2002. Native at 2002 is correct (p7, p11b). Under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD at --std 2002 the compiler keeps 34 digits: IOB(2**110-1) - IOB(2**110-2) = 1, where a 32-digit standard intermediate gives 0 (p11c); at 37 digits (2**120) it gives 0 (p11). This is the KNOWN 32-vs-34-digit standard-arithmetic defect reaching this rule, not a new one.

2002 8.5.2.1: 'An alphabetic data item may be specified wherever an elementary alphanumeric data item is permitted as an operand.' So in 2002 a PIC A(8) item (2002 also lets it hold any alphanumeric characters) is a legal LOCALE-DATE argument-1 'of class alphanumeric'. 2023 8.5.2.2 has no such sentence; 2014 E.2 item 2 records the removal as a substantive change affecting existing programs ('may be used only where rules explicitly allow them'). Second case: a PIC 9(8) USAGE NATIONAL item is class national under 2002 8.5.2.7 item 3 (as for LOCALE-COMPARE). Compiler at --std 2002 is WRONG for the alphabetic case: COBOL1627 'argument-1 is of class alphabetic' (probe a1; expected: accepted, date formatted); it also rejects the numeric-national case (probe n2).
